title: Choose the visual world for KKN Travels
question: The roll assigned Dubai Wayfinding. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dubai Wayfinding
options.lineage: UAE road and street-name signs, Arabic above English
options.thesis: The site is the sign: every errand gets a bilingual direction panel that points you to the right counter.
options.viewport: A sign-blue field fills the screen: one huge bilingual headline, Arabic above English, and direction panels pointing to Visas, Flights, Attestation and Holidays.
options.risk: Can read as government or novelty if the panels are copied literally instead of refined.

raised.raise: One control re-rigs the whole page: the language switch trades Arabic and English places and flips every arrow.
The sign colour owns the entire first viewport, not a panel floating on white.
One sign-scale phrase carries the headline; everything else stays small at the margins.
One calm white panel holds the only form in the first viewport.
Panels stack in gantry order with real overlap, never a flat grid of cards.

options.label: Departures Board
options.thesis: Every service is a row on the board: the errand, what to bring, how long it takes, which counter.
options.viewport: A full-width board of service rows that flap into place, ending in a WhatsApp counter column.
options.case: Holds clarity: fixed columns make services scannable. Loses on identification: a concourse board belongs to any city, not Dubai. It also topped my own list before the roll.
options.risk: The flap board is travel's best-known trope, and a black board reads heavy on a phone in daylight.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: A flat plane that one pull gathers into a shaped form.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers into service pleats when the cord is pulled.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nobody sorting a visa identifies with couture, and the offer hides behind the gesture.
options.risk: Beautiful and unreadable as a travel desk.
options.kept: One control that visibly transforms the whole form.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.thesis: Services orbit a dark centre on warped light rings.
options.viewport: A glowing disk with service labels riding its rings.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an irreversible threshold is the wrong story for a visa application, and labels on curves cost clarity.
options.risk: Spectacle with no errand in it.
options.kept: Total commitment of one colour field to the whole frame.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living shader fills the screen with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: One huge word over a breathing colour field, links in the corners.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it hides the service list and is heavy on the low-end phones this audience uses.
options.risk: Reads as an agency showreel, not a place to get a visa.
options.kept: The scale courage of one oversized phrase against small margins.

options.label: Festival Hoarding
options.thesis: A loud paper collage with one calm white ticket panel on top.
options.viewport: Stacked colour-per-letter headline over a cut-paper city, a white finder card floating above.
options.case: Fuses poorly: festival loudness undercuts the trust a passport handover needs.
options.risk: Fun for holidays, wrong for immigration paperwork.
options.kept: One calm white panel as the single place to act.

options.label: Torn Billboard
options.thesis: Layers of old posters torn through, the tears as composition.
options.viewport: Fragments of four type systems exposed through ragged tears.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no fragment is complete, and this audience needs complete answers fast.
options.kept: Real layering and overlap order instead of a flat grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Dubai travel agencies ship: skyline photo, navy and gold, icon service cards, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed Dubai skyline photo with a headline, two buttons and a row of service cards beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
